title: The winter cold tongue and slope current off southern Vietnam
query: Using the supplied CMOMS daily temperature and velocity for 2011-2020, test the following findings of Liu et al. (2004, Journal of Geophysical Research, doi:10.1029/2003JC002179) on the South China Sea in boreal winter: (1) the Indo-Pacific warm pool has a gap over the South China Sea, where a cold tongue off southern Vietnam keeps sea surface temperature well below that of the surrounding waters; (2) an intense southward slope current south of Vietnam, exceeding 0.5 m/s and forming the western boundary current of the winter cyclonic gyre, creates the cold tongue by advecting cold water from the north; (3) the slope current and the cold tongue are strongest from November to February; (4) the cold tongue's interannual variability follows ENSO, warming during El Nino as the winter monsoon weakens and the circulation spins down. No ENSO index is supplied; you may use published ENSO event classifications. Give a verdict for each finding (reproduced, partly reproduced, not reproduced, or not testable with the supplied data) with quantitative evidence, and explain differences from the paper, which used satellite data.

paper.title: A gap in the Indo‐Pacific warm pool over the South China Sea in boreal winter: Seasonal development and interannual variability
